veranderings.rede: A span of generations is idiomatically 'oor ... heen'; bare 'oor baie geslagte' reads as 'about many generations'.
'hulle versier' after 'mense gewerk' can read as decorating some other thing; 'hulself' makes the reflexive clear.

veranderings.voor: Die prente wys mense wat jag en dans, en ook dinge wat hulle geglo het.
veranderings.na: Die prente wys mense wat jag en dans. Hulle wys ook dinge wat die mense geglo het.
veranderings.rede: AWS allows no comma before 'en' within one sentence, and dropping it makes 'jag en dans en ook dinge' ambiguous, so split into two sentences.

veranderings.voor: Navorsers leer ook deur mense wat vandag leef dop te hou
veranderings.na: Navorsers leer ook meer deur mense wat vandag leef, dop te hou
veranderings.rede: 'leer ook' needs an object to read naturally, and a comma after the embedded relative clause helps a Grade 5 reader find the verb.

veranderings.na: dus wys hierdie navorsing nie presies
veranderings.rede: 'dit' has no clear antecedent (leefwyses is plural); naming the research makes the reference clear.

veranderings.na: saam vertel hulle ons die meeste
veranderings.rede: 'vertel' without an indirect object sounds unfinished here.

veranderings.voor: wat ons oor nou en oor lank gelede vertel
veranderings.na: wat ons van vandag en van lank gelede vertel
veranderings.rede: 'oor nou' is unidiomatic; 'vertel van vandag en van lank gelede' is natural Afrikaans with the same meaning.
'groep' alone is vague and the following 'hulle' needs people as its referent.

vlae.teks: Rotskuns of rotstekeninge is prente wat mense op rotse geskilder of in die klip ingekerf het.
vlae.rede: The protected decision for 'rotskuns' says 'prente' was avoided because a later lesson teaches that herders' rock art is geometric patterns 'in plaas van prente'; this study sentence still defines rock art as 'prente'. Content question for the writer, not changed.

vlae.teks: Voorwerpe (artefakte) is dinge wat mense gemaak of gebruik het.
vlae.rede: The study text says artefacts are things people made or USED, while the glossary says made or ALTERED; a learner gets two answers in one lesson. Content question, not changed.
